prompt: What is a defining trait of the Lettuce client compared with Jedis?
explanation: Lettuce is built on Netty: its RedisConnection is thread-safe and can be shared across threads, and it exposes synchronous, asynchronous (CompletableFuture), and reactive APIs. Jedis uses a blocking per-connection model and has no reactive API.

options.text: Its connection is thread-safe and shareable, with sync, async, and reactive APIs
It talks a different wire protocol than every other Redis client
It only supports string values and cannot pipeline commands
It requires one dedicated connection per thread, like Jedis
